name: GANGES CHASMA — Valles Marineris wall
blurb: The steepest wall section the terrain scan could find in the eastern Valles Marineris. Descent by switchback, on talus.

meta.citation: ESA Mars Express HRSC + NASA MGS MOLA blended global DEM, 200 m/px, v2
meta.grid: azimuthal equidistant about the site, resampled bilinear, long axis on bearing 39 deg
meta.resolution_note: source product is 200 m/px; this 1024x512 grid at 4 m/px spans 20 x 10 source posts and is a 50x bilinear resampling of them — interpolation, not added detail
meta.layout: row-major, +x along the traverse, +y to its left
meta.note: Steep descent by switchback. Chosen for the steepest wall section the scan can find.

lope.label: LOPE
lope.blurb: The gait the Apollo crews adopted within minutes on every mission. One foot at a time, airborne between every step — a walk whose double support has been replaced by flight.

bound.label: BOUND
bound.blurb: Both feet together, everything into the vertical. The robot is identical on all three bodies and pushes identically, so the whole difference in height and hang is the field.

trip.label: TRIP + RECOVER
trip.blurb: A caught toe, and the fall that follows. Toppling is a pendulum about the toe, so the time to go over scales as 1/sqrt(g): 0.93 s on Earth against 2.28 s on the Moon. That extra second and a third is what the Apollo crews used to get a hand down.
